conventions.convention: Inner products are linear in the first argument. The energy-basis amplitude is Aji(t,s)=exp(iEj(t−s)/ħ)〈U(t,s)φi,φj〉; its interaction-picture expression includes exp(is(Ei−Ej)/ħ).

The three propagation classes are bounded norm-continuous, strongly continuous bounded control added to a fixed self-adjoint operator, and self-adjoint common-domain C¹(Y,H) evolution. Bounded-control evolution is mild and carries no domain-invariance assertion. On a singleton time interval only U(a,a)=I is asserted.

Physical time is in seconds, energies in joules, ħ remains explicit, and ω0, Ω1 and ω have units s⁻¹. Detuning is Δ=ω0−ω. Circular and linear drive Hamiltonians have the distinct coefficients specified in clause (f).
The rotating state is ψR=Rψ with R=cos(ωt/2)I+i sin(ωt/2)σz. Its generator is RHR*+iħR′R*. Circular driving gives transverse coefficient Ω1; averaging the linear drive gives Ω1/2.
Dyson truncations act on the initial unit vector without renormalization; their quadratic spectral estimates need not be probability measures.

Slow time s lies in [0,1], physical time is t=sT with T>0 in seconds, and iħ∂sUT=TH(s)UT. A followed spectral projection must be norm-continuous and uniformly separated from its complement. Leakage concerns the entire followed subspace.
The Coulomb protocol follows the whole n²-dimensional eigenspace for a prescribed positive C² coupling path, with fixed mass and ħ; its normalized slow parameter is S=Tħ/(2m).

load_bearing.statement: The driven model prescribes a self-adjoint energy family in one of three stated regularity classes, its unitary two-time evolution, evolved preparations and outcome readings, energy-basis amplitudes, and the circular and linear two-level drive families.

For the specified Pauli frame R, the transformed circular generator is (ħ/2)(Δσz+Ω1σx); the transformed linear generator is A+exp(2iωt)B+exp(−2iωt)B*, with A=(ħ/2)(Δσz+(Ω1/2)σx), B=(ħΩ1/8)(σx+iσy). The transformed propagator is R(t)U(t,s)R(s)* and level populations are invariant.

In the declared bounded norm-continuous class the Dyson sum is the unique unitary propagator; for τ=|t−s|, its order-N remainder is bounded by exp(Kτ)(Kτ)^(N+1)/(N+1)!, and the unnormalized truncated quadratic outcome estimate differs from the exact Born probability by at most 2exp(Kτ)(Kτ)^(N+1)/(N+1)!.

For self-adjoint H0 and a strongly continuous uniformly bounded self-adjoint control V, the declared model has a unique unitary mild propagator, interaction-picture strong evolution and identical outcome laws under simultaneous transport of states and bounded observables; no invariance of D(H0) is asserted.

For the declared bounded-control model and an orthonormal eigenfamily, Aji=δij+Aji^(1)+Rji with |Rji|≤exp(Kτ)(Kτ)²/2. The stated sinusoidal decomposition and transition/survival probability error bounds hold at finite times.

For the declared circular drive, Uc(t,s)=R(t)*exp(−i(t−s)(Δσz+Ω1σx)/2)R(s). Starting in the up level, the down-population is Ω1² sin²(b(t−s)/2)/b² for b>0, with b²=Δ²+Ω1²; Ω1=0 gives constant populations.

For the declared linear drive with ω≠0, the rotated propagator differs from exp(−i(t−s)A/ħ) by at most ε(τ)=|Ω1|/(2|ω|)[1+τ(|Δ|/2+3|Ω1|/4)], τ=|t−s|. The down-population differs from the averaged Rabi population by at most 2ε(τ).

For the declared self-adjoint common-domain C¹(Y,H) family, the unique strong propagator preserves Y with a uniform graph bound and the stated endpoint equations. The driven oscillator Hosc−f(t)Q with real C¹ f satisfies these hypotheses.

The declared finite or common-domain slow protocol has duration T>0, equation iħ∂sUT=TH(s)UT, a uniformly gapped coherently followed spectral projection, and Born leakage probability ||(I−P(s))UT(s,0)ψ(0)||² for a unit initial vector in ran P(0).

concerns.concern: Proof 1.2 says 'the case N=0 gives' ||U−I||≤exp(Kτ)−1, citing F2. Substitution into F2 gives exp(Kτ)Kτ, or the stronger Kτ, rather than the stated expression. F1 explicitly supplies exp(Kτ)−1, so the conclusion is sound but this step should cite F1.

The Teschl reference describes Chapter 5 pp.123–131 as supplying 'the Dyson expansion'. The retrieved 2009 chapter covers autonomous groups, RAGE and Trotter instead. The local Dyson suppliers support the deduction. Source: [Teschl](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/schroe.pdf), Chapter 5.

The Teschl reference attributes 'the relation between the Schroedinger and interaction pictures' to Chapter 5 pp.123–131. Its picture discussion on p.130 is Heisenberg, not interaction. The local interaction-picture supplier supports the definition. Source: [Teschl](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/schroe.pdf), p.130.

The Teschl reference describes Chapter 5 pp.123–131 as treating 'mild evolution equations and the interaction picture for a bounded time-dependent perturbation'. That chapter treats autonomous dynamics. The explicit local mathematical supplier supports the proof. Source: [Teschl](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/schroe.pdf), Chapter 5.

The Teschl reference describes Chapter 5 pp.123–131 as treating 'the harmonic oscillator and its coherent states'. The contents instead locate the oscillator in §8.3, p.178. The example has explicit local suppliers. Source: [Teschl](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~gerald/ftp/book-schroe/schroe.pdf), contents and Chapter 5.

The Example quantifies over every s,t∈[a,b], but L1's explicit-propagator supplier states its response/factorization for s≤t. The proof applies it without explaining the reverse-time extension. Extending the zero-data forced solution backward and checking the same factorization by differentiation and uniqueness closes this small gap.

Clause (d) and Verification 2.1 say that at τ=0 'the two propagators coincide while the bound is 1/50'. Here the propagator bound ε(0) is 1/100; 1/50 is the population-difference bound 2ε(0). Specify which bound is meant.

alerts.finding: The page summary says ex-nrqm-light-matter-two-level-dipole-drive-check 'computes the resonant co-rotating first-order amplitude dE0τ/(2ħ)'. The example's clause (b) correctly states this as |a+|. With its declared W=−dE0σx and initial time zero, the complex amplitude is i dE0τ/(2ħ). The summary should preserve the modulus distinction.

seams_checked.note: Contextual ordering prerequisite; no stationary perturbation or WKB result is silently used as a driven or adiabatic theorem.
P1/P2/P4 and unit conventions are retained; prescribed driving is explicitly an additional model assumption beyond autonomous P4.
Unit rays, positive trace-one densities and unitary transport retain their stated meanings.
Sharp outcomes use spectral projection probabilities; truncated quadratic estimates are explicitly unnormalized, and empirical records are excluded.
The free group is exp(−itH0/ħ); its unbounded-domain differentiation is not transferred to the merely mild driven evolution.
Density expansions and projection probabilities are used under their choice hypotheses; supported mixed-state leakage follows by weighting pure-state bounds.

Actual supplier statements preserve latest-time-left Dyson ordering, strong vector integrals, common-domain regularity and finite-time error bounds. The amplitude theorem locally proves its extension from a complete eigenbasis to a fixed eigenpair.
Pauli matrices, basis order and linear-first pairing agree with clause (e) of the finite-spin supplier.
The exact oscillator energy and maximal position operator are retained; driving is explicitly added as a separate model assumption.
The Coulomb energies, n² degeneracy and essential interval are preserved. The protocol follows the entire eigenspace and adds a prescribed source-strength path.
The infinitesimal kinetic bound is applied on the exact H² domain to establish uniform graph equivalence and C² family regularity.
Pauli actions and raising/lowering combinations agree with the supplier.
Numerical frequency substitutions have explicit units; coupling ratios and elapsed-time products are dimensionless model data.
Populations, preparation means and separate position/momentum spreads are model probabilities and moments, not recorded observations or joint outcome laws.
Initial and transported vectors are normalized pure preparations; scalar phases are removed only from phase-invariant quantities.
Free coherent rotation, means and spreads match the cited evolution and fluctuation statements.

The oscillator example uses the explicit displacement identities faithfully, but extends the supplier's forward-time factorization to all endpoint orders without explaining the reverse-time extension; recorded as a small gap in concerns.

The dipole-drive definition supplies continuous finite matrices; the stimulated-transition theorem preserves the amplitude phases, Dyson tail, Ω1=−2dE0/ħ identification and ω≠0 condition for the linear-drive error contract.

The two-level example correctly retains the averaged Rabi formula and error contract and distinguishes full first-order from co-rotating coefficients. Its page summary calls the amplitude modulus the amplitude; routed in alerts.
